title: Audible vs Kindle Unlimited UK: which subscription is worth it?
seoTitle: Audible vs Kindle Unlimited UK 2026: Which Is Worth It?
description: Audible vs Kindle Unlimited in the UK: prices, what you get, who each suits, and today's offers (Audible £0.99 a month to 17 Dec, KU 30 days free).
intro:
**Short answer: pick Audible if you want to listen and keep your books, and Kindle Unlimited if you read lots of ebooks and are happy to borrow. Right now Audible is £0.99 a month for three months plus a £10 bonus for eligible members (until 17 December), and Kindle Unlimited has a 30-day free trial, then £9.49 a month.**

Trying both before Christmas costs under £3. Below are the two offers, today's Amazon prices on Kindles to read on and earbuds to listen with (TechRadar, 24 and 25 November 2026), and a straight comparison to help you choose.

body:
## The quick verdict

- **Best overall for most people: Audible**, if you like to listen. The Black Friday offer (£0.99 a month for three months, plus a £10 bonus for eligible members, until 17 December) is the cheapest it gets.
- **Best cheap: Kindle Unlimited**, if you read a lot of genre fiction. The 30-day trial is free and it works in the free Kindle app.
- **Best splurge: a Kindle Paperwhite at £134.99** with Kindle Unlimited on it, or a Kindle Scribe at £314.99 if you also want to write notes.

## The difference in one line

**Audible is for listening and you keep what you buy. Kindle Unlimited is for reading and you borrow.** That's the whole decision for most people.

- **What it is:** Audible is audiobooks. Kindle Unlimited is ebooks, with free narration on some titles.
- **Normal UK price:** Audible Standard £5.99 a month or Premium Plus £8.99 a month. Kindle Unlimited £9.49 a month.
- **Offer now:** Audible £0.99 a month for three months plus a £10 bonus (eligible members, until 17 December). Kindle Unlimited 30 days free.
- **Do you keep the books?** Audible: yes, anything bought with a credit. Kindle Unlimited: no, you borrow up to 20 at a time.
- **Catalogue:** Audible credits work on almost any audiobook, plus the Plus Catalogue. Kindle Unlimited has a few million titles, mostly indie and genre fiction.
- **Need a Kindle?** Neither. Both work in free phone apps.

## Choose Audible if...

- You have a commute, a dog to walk, or chores to get through. Audiobooks fit time when your eyes are busy.
- You want new releases and big names. Audible's credits work on almost any audiobook, including this year's bestsellers, which Kindle Unlimited mostly doesn't carry.
- You like owning things. Books you buy with a credit stay in your library even after you cancel.

The catch is that one credit is one book a month. If you get through four audiobooks a month you'll run out, though the Plus Catalogue gives you a rotating set to listen to without spending credits.

## Choose Kindle Unlimited if...

- You read fast and read a lot: romance, thrillers, fantasy and series fiction are where it shines.
- You're happy to try authors you haven't heard of. Most of the catalogue is self-published or from smaller publishers, and most chart bestsellers aren't in it.
- You want to cut your book spending. At £9.49 a month it pays for itself if you'd otherwise buy two or three ebooks.

Kindle Unlimited is a library, not a shop. Cancel and the books go back. It also includes some titles with free Audible narration, so it's a small taste of both.

## Can you have both?

Yes, and plenty of readers do: Kindle Unlimited for evening reading and Audible for the commute. Right now it costs very little to try them side by side, because the Audible offer is £2.97 for three months and the Kindle Unlimited trial is free. Just set reminders, as both renew automatically at the full price.

If you already pay for Amazon Prime, try Prime Reading first. It's a smaller rotating selection of ebooks included with Prime at no extra cost, and it may be all a light reader needs. Not a member? Start an [Amazon Prime free trial](/guides/amazon-prime-free-trial-black-friday-2026/) and you'll also get Black Friday Week member prices.

## Which Kindle to use it on

You don't need a Kindle for either, but reading on a phone gets tiring. Today's Amazon prices (TechRadar, 25 November) are good:

- **Kindle (2026) at £119.99** is the sensible buy for most people, and it plays Audible over Bluetooth.
- **Paperwhite (2024) at £134.99** is the better screen for only £15 more. That's an easy recommendation for heavy readers.
- **Kindle Kids at £119.99** includes its own kids' book subscription, so you don't need Kindle Unlimited for children.

For a full rundown of models, see our [Kindle Black Friday deals](/guides/kindle-black-friday-deals-2026/) and [Kindle vs Kindle Paperwhite](/guides/kindle-vs-kindle-paperwhite/). Buying for someone else? Our [gifts for book lovers](/guides/gifts-for-book-lovers-uk/) has more ideas, and there's more in our [Christmas gift guides](/christmas-gifts/) and [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/).

## FAQs

### Is Audible or Kindle Unlimited better value?

It depends how you read. For heavy ebook readers who like genre fiction, Kindle Unlimited at £9.49 a month is the better value. For listeners, or anyone who wants new bestsellers, Audible is better because the credits work on almost anything and you keep the books.

### Does Kindle Unlimited include Audible?

No. They're separate subscriptions. Some Kindle Unlimited ebooks come with free Audible narration you can switch to, but it isn't a full Audible membership and you don't get credits.

### How much is Audible a month in the UK?

Audible Standard is £5.99 a month and Premium Plus is £8.99 a month. Until 17 December, eligible members can get three months for £0.99 a month plus a £10 bonus. See our [Audible free trial guide](/guides/audible-free-trial-deals-uk/) for the details and how to cancel.

### Can I cancel Kindle Unlimited during the free trial?

Yes. Go to Memberships and Subscriptions in your Amazon account and end it. You keep access until the trial would have ended, then the borrowed books are returned. Our [Kindle Unlimited free trial guide](/guides/kindle-unlimited-free-trial-uk/) explains the steps.

### Do I need a Kindle for Audible or Kindle Unlimited?

No. Audible works in its app on any phone, and Kindle Unlimited works in the free Kindle app on phones, tablets and computers. A Kindle just makes reading easier on the eyes.
